issues.failure_explanation: The proof asserts that for $C \neq 0$, the real part of the roots of equation (3.16) is $\text{Re}(z) = \frac{1/3+13C}{6C}$. This incorrectly treats the discriminant term $\pm \sqrt{(1/3+13C)^2 - 24C}$ as purely imaginary. In reality, for any $C < 0$, the product of the roots of the quadratic equation is $1 / (\frac{3}{2}C) = \frac{2}{3C} < 0$. Because the product of the roots is negative, the discriminant is strictly positive, both roots are real, and they have opposite signs: one root is strictly positive and one root is strictly negative. Thus, for every $C < -1/39$, there is a negative real root with $\text{Re}(z) < 0$, which places a pole of $G(z)$ in the closed left half-plane $\text{Re}(z) \leq 0$. The claimed equivalence 'if and only if $C \geq 0$ or $C < -1/39$' is false, and all roots lie in the open right half-plane if and only if $C \geq 0$.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the calculation of $\text{Re}(z)$ to account for the real roots when the discriminant is positive, and restrict the necessary and sufficient condition in Lemma 3.2 to $C \geq 0$.
issues.overall_effect: Lemma 3.2 is mathematically false for all $C < -1/39$, where $G(z)$ fails to be analytic in the closed left half-plane. However, the subsequent numerical parameter optimization identifies the operational interval for A-stability as $C \in [0.018824, 0.045589]$, which lies entirely in $C > 0$.
issues.title: Erroneous real part calculation leading to false stability domain in Lemma 3.2
issues.why_classification: Correcting the condition to $C \geq 0$ is a localized, routine repair that preserves the validity of the method, the advertised fourth-order accuracy, and the subsequent A-stability interval, as the operational parameter range $C \in [0.018824, 0.045589]$ is strictly positive.
